2.3 Advertising 
 
A licensed or registered person should ensure that invitations and 
advertisements  do not contain information  that is false, disparaging, 
misleading or deceptive.

Unless otherwise  specified  or the context otherwise  requires, words and 
phrases in the Code shall be interpreted  by reference  to any definition of 
such word or phrase in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the SFO.

This Code does not have the force of law and should not be interpreted  in a 
way that would override the provision of any law.

(a) A licensed or registered  person should, as part of the know 
your client procedures, assess the client’s knowledge of 
derivatives and characterize the client based on his 
knowledge of derivatives.

(b) Where a client without knowledge  of derivatives  wishes to 
purchase a derivative product (he reafter refer to as a 
“transaction” in this paragraph) which is:  
 
(i) traded on an exchange and the licensed or registered 
person has not solicited the client or made a 
recommendation  to the client in relation to the proposed 
transaction, the licensed or regis tered person should 
explain the relevant  risks associated  with the product to 
the client;

missing_premises: Product evidence: the selected product family and its final terms, payoff structure, underlying exposures, legal form, trading venue and offering arrangements are absent. Classification cannot be established from the question’s label alone.

Authority completeness: no complete product-family circular, substantive FAQ answer or complete chain of incorporated definitions, provisions, notes, exceptions and annexes is supplied. The gifts FAQ PDF has no selected text; the selected HTML contains navigation and a concluding fragment rather than the full relevant answers.
Classification branches: the selections do not establish the complete tests, inclusions, exclusions or relationships among structured-product, derivative-product and complex-product classifications.

Advertising branches: paragraph 2.3 supplies a general content standard, but the selections do not settle whether additional product-specific requirements, authorization conditions, exemptions, warnings or restrictions apply to the proposed invitation or advertisement.

Conduct branches: paragraph 5.1A(b)(ii) is incomplete; the complete treatment of off-exchange transactions, solicitation or recommendation, clients with or without derivatives knowledge, and any interaction with suitability requirements remains missing.

Investor exceptions: table-of-contents entries and fragments of professional-investor provisions do not establish which exemptions apply, their conditions, or their effect on the selected product and advertising activity.

Institutional and operational evidence: the issuer’s and distributor’s identities, licensing or registration status, roles, intended recipients, client classifications, actual promotional material, distribution channels and solicitation practices are not supplied.

Temporal applicability: the relevant conduct date and the effective, transitional or supersession provisions governing that date have not been established. Page dates and the filename current-code.pdf do not resolve this.

The supplied JFIU webinar passages concern suspicious-transaction reporting and do not establish structured-product classification or advertising requirements; the JFIU home and login files contain no supplied selections.
next_source_questions: What is the exact selected product family? Supply its final term sheet, offering document and contractual payoff terms so that each classification condition can be tested against identified product features.

Supply the complete official circular and FAQ addressing that family, including their exact titles, scope, attachments, footnotes, incorporated references and amendment or supersession notices. Their identities cannot be established from the supplied selections.

Supply the relevant definitions in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the SFO, together with every provision incorporated by the product-family circular or FAQ that determines classification, exclusions or advertising treatment.

Supply the complete Code application provisions, paragraph 2.3 with any applicable supplementary guidance, paragraph 3.11 and the substantive gifts FAQ answers if promotional gifts are involved, paragraphs 5.1A–5.3, and the full complex-product and professional-investor provisions relevant to the selected family.

Supply the complete official provisions governing invitations, advertisements and offering documents for the identified family, including any authorization requirements, exemptions, required warnings and conditions. Which provisions distinguish the actual offering audience and distribution channel?
What conduct date is being assessed, and which official commencement, amendment and transitional material establishes the applicable version of every included provision?

Supply institutional records establishing the relevant entities’ regulatory status and roles, the proposed advertisement and distribution plan, and records supporting any client classification, exemption, derivatives-knowledge assessment or absence of solicitation relied upon.

Once those sources and facts are supplied, can the complete source slice be frozen and every classification, conduct, advertising and exemption branch mapped to an exact provision and factual predicate, with unresolved predicates retained explicitly before coding?
value.proposition: Express provision: Code paragraph 2.3 states that a licensed or registered person should ensure that invitations and advertisements do not contain false, disparaging, misleading or deceptive information. The supplied portion of paragraph 5.1A expressly requires assessment of clients’ derivatives knowledge and states a risk-explanation requirement for a client without that knowledge purchasing an exchange-traded derivative product without solicitation or recommendation. The off-exchange branch is truncated. The Code also expressly refers interpretation to definitions in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the SFO unless otherwise specified or required by context, and states that it does not have the force of law. Inference: these provisions identify relevant advertising and investor-characterization requirements to investigate, but do not establish the selected product’s classification or the complete advertising regime. Assumptions: this proposal assesses only the supplied selections; the selected product family, relevant conduct date, institution and distribution circumstances remain unspecified; structured products, derivative products and complex products are not assumed to be interchangeable classifications. The complete official circular, FAQ and incorporated provisions have not been supplied. The retained question therefore remains open, and the closure test—freezing the complete source slice and enumerating every applicable branch before coding—is not satisfied. File names, hashes, publication and downloading do not establish completeness or applicability.
